name: Apache Guacamole
description: A clientless, open-source web gateway to your existing RDP/VNC/SSH/Telnet servers — install it once on a server, and anyone reaches those endpoints through nothing but an HTTPS browser tab, with centralized auth, session recording, and no per-host client install.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Guacamole doesn't capture screens itself — it proxies your existing RDP/VNC server, so Wayland support depends on that backend

Tailscale Support.comment: No native integration, though putting Guacamole behind Tailscale/Cloudflare Tunnel is a common security recommendation

Open Source.comment: Apache Software Foundation top-level project, Apache 2.0 license

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: Renders a single monitor in-browser, though the remote resolution updates dynamically as you resize the window

H.264 Codec.comment: Uses its own lightweight instruction protocol to relay backend screen updates, not a video codec

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Depends on the backend server's own capability (e.g. RDS multi-session); Guacamole itself is just the gateway

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: Renders backend RDP/VNC updates as an image stream; fidelity depends on the proxied protocol/server, not Guacamole itself

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: No fixed published figure; performance depends on the backend protocol and network

Session Recording.comment: Records graphical (and optionally keystroke) session activity, with in-browser playback since 1.5.0

Pre-Login Access.comment: Since it proxies RDP/VNC directly, it shows the target's actual login screen like a normal client would

No Account Required.comment: Users must log into the Guacamole web gateway itself before reaching any connection

KVM Integration.comment: Since Guacamole already speaks RDP/VNC, it can proxy into a KVM device's existing VNC/RDP interface, though this isn't a dedicated feature

Shared Clipboard.comment: Bidirectional clipboard sync via the Asynchronous Clipboard API

2FA / MFA.comment: Built-in TOTP since 1.0.0, plus Duo, RADIUS, and YubiKey extension support

Windows: Host.comment: Reachable as an RDP/VNC target; the Guacamole server itself (guacd) is typically deployed on Linux

Windows: Client.comment: Any modern browser, no software install needed

macOS: Host.comment: Reachable as a VNC/SSH target; the Guacamole server itself isn't natively deployed on macOS

Linux X11: Host.comment: Native deployment platform for the guacd/Tomcat stack, and easily reachable as an X11 VNC/SSH target

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Depends entirely on whichever VNC/RDP server is proxied on the Wayland target

Android: Client.comment: Touch-friendly HTML5 web client works in mobile browsers

Web Browser: Client.comment: This is the entire point of Guacamole — 100% browser-based, zero client install ever required

NVIDIA RTX 4090.comment: A protocol gateway, not a GPU-accelerated streaming client

Free Tier.comment: Completely free and open source, no tiers or paid unlocks at all

Enterprise.comment: No official paid tier; some third parties sell managed hosting/support around it, not from the Apache project itself
